improvised.summary: Four measures that echo the shape of the tune, pass through a diminished chord, and pause on D7 before the first note.

measures.note: A small turn around the note D over a rising G arpeggio.
The line reaches the high G over C; the bass then rises a half step to C sharp diminished.
The diminished chord resolves to G over D, and the line walks down to G.
Two chords in thirds, A minor nine and D7, leave the ear waiting for G.

arrangements.name: One step further
arrangements.summary: Same chords as the score. The arpeggio reaches a tenth, and the left hand rolls in eighths whenever the melody holds a long note.
tips: Practise the left hand alone at tempo 60 until the reach from the fifth to the tenth feels relaxed.
In measures 7 and 15 the melody stands still, so let the left hand sing there and keep it quiet elsewhere.

patterns.name: Tenth arpeggio
patterns.description: Root, fifth, then the third one octave up instead of the root. One changed note makes the chord sound open and warm.

patterns.name: Rolling eighths
patterns.description: Climb through the chord in eighth notes and turn back at the top. Use it while the melody holds a long note.

measures.note: Tenth arpeggio: the last note is 3' instead of 1'.
Your usual pattern, so the new one stands out against it.
The melody holds one note for five beats, so the left hand takes over the movement.
The seventh (7) appears inside the roll and pulls towards G.
Ending on the seventh leads the ear into the C chord.
Single notes only: bass D, then B rising to C, which falls back to B in the last chord.
Close with all three notes together.

arrangements.name: Walking bass
arrangements.summary: A waltz texture: one bass note, then two notes together. Inversions let the bass move by step instead of jumping from root to root.
tips: Play only the first note of every measure and listen to the bass line as a melody of its own.
Keep the two-note chords lighter than the bass note.

patterns.name: Bass and pair
patterns.description: Bass note on the first beat, fifth and octave together on the other beats.

patterns.name: Slash-chord bass
patterns.description: Keep the same pair on top and put the third of the chord in the bass. G/B sits one step below C, so the bass walks.

measures.note: G/B: the bass steps up from G through B to reach C in the next measure.
The bass steps back down from C to B.
Em replaces G: it shares two notes with G, and its bass E walks down to D.
D7/C puts the seventh in the bass. It wants to fall one step, to the B of G/B.
The bass stays on B while the pair changes to include the seventh.
The bass walks E to D and stays there; the last pair holds the two notes that define D7.

arrangements.name: New chords
arrangements.summary: Several printed chords are replaced: a secondary dominant, a suspended chord that resolves, and an Amen ending.
tips: Learn the shell shape 1 7 3' on Em7 first; the A7 in the next measure uses exactly the same shape.
Listen for the single note that moves when Dsus4 turns into D7.

patterns.name: Shell voicing
patterns.description: Root, seventh, and the third one octave up. Three notes are enough to show the whole colour of a seventh chord.

patterns.name: Suspend, then resolve
patterns.description: Hold back the third of the dominant by playing the fourth, then let it fall one step.

patterns.name: Amen ending
patterns.description: Place the IV chord over the home bass note before the final chord, the way a sung Amen closes a hymn.

measures.note: G7/B turns the home chord into a dominant of C and puts the leading note B in the bass.
Em7 stands in for G. The melody notes G and B both belong to it.
A7 is the dominant of D, the chord that follows. The hand shape is the same as in the previous measure.
Dsus4 delays the arrival: the fourth (G) replaces the third.
The suspended G falls to F sharp and the chord finally sounds complete.
The bass arrives home on G, but the chord above is still C. The real ending waits one more measure.
The Amen resolves.

arrangements.name: Alberti bass
arrangements.summary: A classical broken-chord figure in even eighths: lowest note, then the two upper notes in turn.
tips: Practise each chord as a block of three notes before breaking it up.
The first note of every measure is the bass; give it slightly more weight than the rest.
Measures 8 and 9 put the seventh and then the third in the bass. Hear how the bass falls C to B.

patterns.name: Alberti figure in three
patterns.description: The chord close together: lowest note, highest, then middle and highest twice. Six even eighths fill a measure of three.

patterns.name: Open figure
patterns.description: The same idea with the root an octave lower, for a fuller sound on the home chord.

measures.note: Open figure: root at the bottom, third at the top.
Close figure on C, one position for the whole measure.
G with B in the bass, so the bass can step up to D.
D7 with its seventh, C, in the bass. That note must fall to B.
And it does: G over B.

arrangements.name: Gospel waltz
arrangements.summary: Octaves in the bass, a passing diminished chord, and a secondary dominant: the sound of this hymn in a gospel church.
tips: Play the octave with a relaxed, heavy arm and the eighths that follow lightly.
Measures 3 and 4 are the heart of the style: C, C sharp diminished, G over D. Practise them as one gesture.
Let the tempo breathe a little at the end of each line.

patterns.name: Octave and roll
patterns.description: An octave on the first beat, then the upper chord notes as rolling eighths.

patterns.name: Passing diminished chord
patterns.description: Between the four chord and the home chord, the bass rises by half steps: C, C sharp, D.

patterns.name: Secondary dominant
patterns.description: A7 is not in the key of G. It is the dominant of D and makes the arrival on D stronger.

measures.note: G7 over B: the seventh, F, appears and the bass prepares the step to C.
C sharp diminished on the third beat; the melody note E belongs to it.
The diminished chord resolves to G over D.
E minor seven replaces G for the second line of the verse.
A7, the dominant of D. Its C sharp is the note outside the key.
The seventh in the bass again, falling to B.
A minor and D7, the two-five of G, replace G over D.
The bass is home, but the chord above is C: the Amen is on its way.

arrangements.name: Grand octaves
arrangements.summary: A broad, festive accompaniment: an octave in the bass on the first beat and full chords on the other two.
tips: The leap from the octave to the chord is the whole difficulty; practise it slowly and without looking.
Change the pedal on every first beat.
Follow the dynamics so that measure 9 is clearly the loudest point.

patterns.name: Octave and chords
patterns.description: The root in octaves, then the full chord twice. The foundation of a grand hymn accompaniment in three.

patterns.name: Four-note final chord
patterns.description: Root, fifth, octave and tenth together. If the reach is too wide, roll the chord from the bottom.

measures.note: The chord C, D, F sharp adds the seventh; it builds towards the loudest measure.
The final chord spans a tenth.

arrangements.name: Jazz waltz
arrangements.summary: A jazz-waltz reharmonization: a bass note, then a two-note shell, with sixth chords, two-five-one chains, and rootless thirteenths.
tips: The rhythm is bass on one, shell on two, silence on three. Count it aloud before adding the melody.
The shell is the seventh and the third of the chord (written 7 3'). Find it for G6, Em7, A9 and D7 first.
Play quietly; the colour of these chords carries without force.

patterns.name: Bass, then shell
patterns.description: The root on the first beat, the seventh and third together on the second, held through the third.

patterns.name: Two-five-one
patterns.description: D minor and G7 are the second and fifth steps of C; they turn the arrival on C into an event.

patterns.name: Rootless thirteenth
patterns.description: Seventh, third and thirteenth without the root. The melody or the previous bass note supplies the rest.

measures.note: G6 instead of G: the sixth, E, adds warmth without a seventh.
The two-five of C. The melody note B is the thirteenth of D minor.
C major seven, then the passing diminished chord a half step higher.
G6 with D in the bass completes the rise C, C sharp, D.
A9 is the dominant of D; the melody note B is its ninth.
A minor seven delays D7 by a measure and makes a two-five.
On the last beat the chord drops its root and adds the thirteenth, B, the note of the melody.
The two-five of G under the last line of the verse.
The final chord: G with its sixth and ninth.
